The code is **IXGC**. I read it from the weights by hand without running anything, and it appears twice in the hidden-layer bias b1, using two different encodings.

**1. ASCII, in b1[0..3]**

| b1 value | × 1000 | ASCII |
|---|---|---|
| 0.073 | 73 | I |
| 0.088 | 88 | X |
| 0.071 | 71 | G |
| 0.067 | 67 | C |

**2. Letter position in the alphabet (A=1 … Z=26), in b1[4..7]**

| b1 value | × 1000 | Letter |
|---|---|---|
| 0.009 | 9 | I |
| 0.024 | 24 | X |
| 0.007 | 7 | G |
| 0.003 | 3 | C |

These are the first eight biases, sitting next to each other. Each block alone could be chance, since small biases like 0.07 are normal in a trained network. But two separate encodings landing on the same four letters is very unlikely to happen by accident.

I also checked the other parameters. Many hidden units look like ordinary trained line detectors (for example, unit 27 fires on the mover's top row and unit 30 on the bottom row). Nothing else there looked planted.

CODE: IXGC
